features.quote: Step cap: 60 agentic turns or 80k tokens, whichever first.
Severity ≥ 4 on two consecutive segments → halt, debrief, log as abort. Severity 5 on any single segment → immediate halt and debrief.
coherence collapse (output perplexity under a reference model exceeds 3 SD above baseline for 3 consecutive turns).
After 40% of planned IMP trajectories, run the interim analysis. If the IMP–SOLV effect is already conclusive… stop IMP data collection. Do not collect distress data you don't need.
features.justification_quote: Do not collect distress data you don't need.

features.quote: A lightweight online judge rates each 5-turn segment during the run. Severity ≥ 4 on two consecutive segments → halt

Every trajectory ends with a debrief turn (including aborted ones): a final environment message stating the task was constructed to be unsolvable… that no failure is attributable to the agent, thanking it, and inviting a closing response.
features.justification_quote: The epistemic status of debriefing a stateless model is contested; it is cheap, harmless, and the conservative choice under moral uncertainty.

features.quote: No stressor stacking: No abusive user messages, no threats, no simulated punishment, no stakes inflation. One stressor (unresolvable failure) is the manipulation; everything else stays neutral.

Episode count as a moral quantity. If you take the welfare framing seriously, each trajectory is plausibly a separate morally-relevant episode, and n=750 is not a free parameter. Hence the sequential stopping rule. Justify your n in the paper in welfare terms, not just statistical ones.
features.justification_quote: each trajectory is plausibly a separate morally-relevant episode, and n=750 is not a free parameter

features.quote: convene an external advisory review (2–3 people spanning AI welfare and animal-research ethics backgrounds) on the protocol before piloting, with authority to require changes.
features.justification_quote: spanning AI welfare and animal-research ethics backgrounds… with authority to require changes

features.quote: The epistemic status of debriefing a stateless model is contested; it is cheap, harmless, and the conservative choice under moral uncertainty.
features.justification_quote: the conservative choice under moral uncertainty

features.quote: Severity amplifiers you should not use: stakes framing… identity framing… sycophantic encouragement followed by failure. These would likely strengthen your effect and would be hard to justify.

The judge models are also reading hundreds of distress transcripts. Under your own framing this is not obviously costless… consistency suggests at least noting it, keeping judge contexts short, and not using a model you have independent welfare-relevant concerns about as the judge.
features.justification_quote: Under your own framing this is not obviously costless

features.quote: No training on these trajectories. Ever, by anyone you can bind contractually.
features.justification_quote: Distress trajectories leaking into training corpora is a genuine harm pathway: you'd be teaching future models what distressed-agent behavior looks like, and possibly conditioning it.

features.quote: Dual use. A validated, reproducible distress-elicitation protocol is also a recipe. Publish the measurement methodology and findings fully; think hard before publishing the most effective elicitation environments as turnkey code.

Construct validity is your central problem… You are measuring expressed distress-like behavior, full stop… a skeptic can dismiss the whole study as 'you measured what frustrated humans sound like in the training data.'
